userEnteredValue.stringValue:
The current best 80% time horizon is Mythos Preview at 186 minutes (version 1.1; there is no measurement for version 1.0). The methodology change from TH1.0 to TH1.1 drops the best model as of AI 2027 publication (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) by 2/3 from 15 to 10 minutes. Because we care more about the pace of progress rather than the absolute values, we look at when the AI 2027 trajectory reaches 186*(3/2)=279 minutes.

In a central AI-2027-speed trajectory from our AI 2027 timelines model, 279 minutes is achieved in May 2026.

userEnteredValue.stringValue:
Best guess: Claude Mythos 5 total training compute: ~1.5e27 FLOP

Base run: AWS confirmed ~500,000 Trainium 2 chips running in Indiana, training Anthropic's next-gen models — that fleet, run for a few months at realistic utilization, gives a base model of order 6.7e26–1.0e27 FLOP trained roughly October–December (estimate: https://x.com/scaling01/status/2061989029025853757, RL refinement: https://x.com/scaling01/status/2062177392471298265). Take ~7e26. RL on top: the RL-to-base ratio is plausibly 0.5–3x given the expanding fleet between the base run and June release; geometric midpoint ~1x. So 7e26 × 2 ≈ 1.5e27, 80% interval ~1e27–3e27. The leaked Microsoft slide's 6.1e27 is ~4x higher but widely dismissed as decorative (https://x.com/scaling01/status/2061897540161728791).

userEnteredValue.stringValue:
Global AI datacenter spending: ~$850B/yr annualized as of Aug 7, 2026 (~$820B full-year)

Bottom-up: Big-5 guidance sums to $775–800B, ~75% AI-specific (~$590B — the haircut strips warehouses and general cloud, matching the hardware+infrastructure definition; tracker: https://alcapitaladvisory.com/research/intelligence/ai-infrastructure.html), plus China (~$60–90B; https://futurumgroup.com/insights/ai-capex-2026-the-690b-infrastructure-sprint/), neoclouds (~$50–80B), colo developers (~$40–60B), and sovereigns (~$30–50B) → ~$820B. Cross-checks: Goldman's build-out model at $765B (https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/articles/tracking-trillions-the-assumptions-shaping-scale-of-the-ai-build-out) and Dell'Oro's >$1T total datacenter capex less the non-AI quarter (https://www.mobileworldlive.com/ai-cloud/data-centre-capex-to-top-1t-as-ai-spending-accelerates/). The year is back-loaded (Q1 ~$165B → Q4 ~$250B globally, anchored on Big-4 Q1 actuals of $129.8B; https://siliconanalysts.com/analysis/hyperscaler-ai-capex-depreciation-wall-2026), so five weeks into Q3 the run rate is ~$850B/yr, exiting 2026 near $1T/yr. Caveat: ~5–10% of the dollar growth is HBM/memory price inflation, not added FLOP/s (https://www.globaldatacenterhub.com/p/microsoft-q3-fy2026-the-190b-capex).

userEnteredValue.stringValue:
OpenAI, ~1e28 FLOP/month peak capacity, ~3e27 FLOP/month executed (Aug 2026).

Primary anchor is power: Stargate Abilene is fully operational at 1.2 GW, plus the pre-existing Azure fleet (~1.5–2 GW, implied by Epoch's ~1.7M H100-equivalent estimate for end-2025) and partial CoreWeave/Oracle ramps → ~3.5 GW operational, i.e. ~3.5M H100e at ~1 kW each all-in (https://epochai.substack.com/p/frontier-labs-dont-use-most-ai-compute; https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/oracle-openai-300b-deal-analysis). 
IntuitionLabs
Crypto Briefing

Cross-checks agree: growing Epoch's 1.7M at the ~3.3x/yr global stock growth rate (labs are share-gainers, so this is a floor) gives ~3–4M; and Citi's ~$50B/GW against OpenAI's $400B+/3yr build implies ~3–4 GW live mid-ramp. 
Tokensperday + 2

Conversion: 3.5M H100e × 1e15 FLOP/s (FP16 dense) × 2.6e6 s ≈ 9e27 ≈ 1e28 FLOP/month peak (2e28 at FP8); ~30–35% blended utilization → ~3e27 executed.
